# Embedded, automotive, and industrial

## Scope

Applies when the change touches firmware, vehicles, connected devices, OT. Not when the software runs only on servers or phones, with no device, vehicle, or plant control. Neighbours: `aidd-team:secure-coding`, `aidd-team:release-rollout`, `aidd-team:threat-model`.

## Terms

- **ASIL and SIL**: The integrity level the safety analysis assigns; it sets the rigour of the whole life cycle.
- **Safe state**: The state the system falls back to on a fault.
- **Functional safety, SOTIF, and cybersecurity**: Three analyses: failures, an insufficient intended function, and attacks.
- **OTA update**: A signed software update delivered over the air, with rollback protection.
- **Product with digital elements**: The Cyber Resilience Act's term for hardware or software with a data connection.

## Dated obligations

| From | Obligation | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2024-07-07 | UN R155 and R156 apply to existing EU whole-vehicle type approvals (categories M and N), not only to new types. | S5 |
| 2025-08-01 | The RED delegated act's cybersecurity requirements apply to internet-connected radio equipment. EN 18031-1, -2, and -3:2024 are written for that act. Check their Official Journal listing before claiming presumption of conformity. | S8 |
| 2026-09-11 | CRA reporting applies: an actively exploited vulnerability or a severe incident goes to the single reporting platform, on the clocks in `aidd-team:incident-response`. | S7 |
| 2027-12-11 | The CRA's main obligations apply (essential requirements, vulnerability handling, conformity assessment, CE marking), and the RED delegated act is repealed. | S7, S8 |

## Invariants and missed cases

| Always true | The case a plan misses |
| --- | --- |
| Every fault ends in a defined safe state. | A power loss during an update, or a watchdog reset loop. |
| An update installs only when it is signed and newer. | A downgrade to a vulnerable version, or a half-written image. |
| Timing budgets hold in the worst case, not the average. | A new log line in an interrupt handler. |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | Safety-related code is major with the security pool; name the safety integrity level (ASIL, SIL) the change touches. | S2, S3 |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | A product with digital elements sold in the EU is in CRA scope. Name whether it is an important (class I or II) or critical product, and its support period. Name whether a radio makes the RED delegated act apply until 2027-12-11. | S7, S8 |
| Specify | Requirements trace to tests; timing, memory, and power budgets in the Acceptance; failure modes and safe states named. | S2, S3 |
| Specify | A vehicle change names its effect on type approval: the cyber security risk assessment (R155). For an update, also the target versions, dependency checks, and update record (R156, ISO 24089). | S5 |
| Specify | A perception or driver-assistance change names its triggering conditions and performance limits, and how the scenarios that cover them are validated (SOTIF). | S6 |
| Implement | MISRA-compliant code with documented deviations; no dynamic allocation after init where the standard forbids it; secure boot and update paths untouched or re-verified. | S1, S4 |
| Implement | No universal default password; a vulnerability-disclosure contact; signed updates with rollback protection; an SBOM from the build. | S8, S7 |
| Review | Static analysis clean; hardware-in-the-loop results where the project has a rig, otherwise simulation or model results, and the Spec says which. | S1, S2 |
| Ship | Staged fleet rollout with a rollback image; fault and reset telemetry as the observe signals. | S2, S5 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MISRA and static analysis | no rule violation without a documented deviation | Cppcheck (2.22.0) with the MISRA addon, Clang-Tidy, or a qualified tool | S1 |
| Coverage at the required level | statement, branch, or MC/DC coverage as the standard requires | the unit test runner with coverage thresholds | S2, S3 |
| HIL or simulation run | the changed behavior holds on hardware or a model | the HIL rig in CI where the project has one, otherwise the simulator or model; the Spec says which | S2 |
| Firmware signing test | an unsigned, tampered, or older (rollback) image is rejected | a test of the update path | S4, S5 |
| Protocol fuzzing | every parser and protocol handler survives malformed input | libFuzzer or AFL++ on the handlers | S4 |
| Default credential and open port check | the built image has no universal default password and listens only on the ports the Spec names | a test that boots the image on the rig or in an emulator, lists its listening ports against the Spec's allow-list, and tries the factory credentials | S8, S7 |

- From `aidd-team:enterprise-controls`: Container scan and SBOM.

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/roles.json`.
